Francesco Craighero

Senior Computational Biologist in the Single Cell Genomics Group at CNAG, Barcelona

CNAG, Barcelona, Spain

I am a Senior Computational Biologist in the Single Cell Genomics Group led by Holger Heyn at CNAG in Barcelona. My research focuses on machine learning for molecular and cellular data, from building and querying single-cell atlases of inflammation to predicting ribosome dynamics along mRNA sequences, and on making these models more reliable and interpretable.

Before joining CNAG, I was at EPFL, working with the Signal Processing Laboratory 2 (LTS2) and the Naef Lab. I obtained my PhD in Computer Science at the University of Milano-Bicocca, with a thesis on anomaly detection in deep learning, covering the interpretability of activation patterns, adversarial example detection and out-of-distribution detection. During my PhD, I spent six months as a visiting researcher at IBM Research Zurich.
